flows:
Navigate to https://guest-it.vercel.app then A visitor reports a bug in the web app at https://guest-it.vercel.app . Their report, in their own words: "If I type an address that does not exist, like /this-page-does-not-exist, I get the raw error page of the host instead of the own not-found page of the app with a way back home."
Do what the report describes, the way a normal visitor would.
Rules: read-only.
Do not sign in, do not create an account, do not submit any form that sends data, do not buy anything.
Assert that the reported bug is really present: what the report says goes wrong does go wrong.

verdict.root_cause: After opening the made-up address, the automation waited for the "Admin Login" heading and its browser address became /login. The final check therefore examined the login screen rather than the invalid address.
verdict.agent_fault_assessment: The agent caused the failed verification by changing its verification target from the requested invalid path to the login state. Step 0-2 shows the invalid-path request returned successfully, while step 0-3 explicitly waited for "Admin Login" and records the URL as https://guest-it.vercel.app/login. The screenshots likewise show the normal portal and then the app's Admin Login screen, not a raw host error page. Thus the asserted condition was unsupported and the reported behavior was not reproduced.
